posts.engagement_rate_source: LinkedIn's own 'Post performance' panel (Page posts -> Preview results -> Show all results), not manually recomputed -- their formula is authoritative and may weight fields (e.g. clicks) differently than a naive reactions+comments+shares/impressions calc.
posts.notes: DRY RUN reading, not a real nightly check. posts.notes: Scheduled automation (/orl-publish --fire) failed to actually fire on 09-08: found two bugs, (1) both scheduled tasks pointed at bare 'claude' which Task Scheduler couldn't resolve -- fixed, (2) the standalone claude.exe CLI's OAuth login had expired -- fixed with an API key. Published manually instead, roughly 11 hours after the intended 00:00 slot. DO NOT mark 00:00 as tried in timing-intelligence/state.json based on this entry -- the actual post time diverged too far from the assigned slot to say anything about how 00:00 itself performs. Checked late (09-10, ~2 days after posting, not the usual same-day-later reading) because /orl-timing --log-previous had no working browser mechanism until linkedin-bot.py was built.

posts.engagement_rate_source: socials/scripts/linkedin-bot.py --analytics (standalone Playwright script reading LinkedIn's own Post performance panel)
posts.notes: Scheduled ORL-Fire ran at 00:30 (Task Scheduler exit 0) but did nothing -- root cause was a stale OAuth credential file (~/.claude/.credentials.json) blocking claude.exe from ever falling back to ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in headless mode, compounded by insufficient API balance underneath that. Both fixed (credential file renamed to .bak, balance topped up). Fired manually via /orl-publish --fire run directly in an interactive session instead of retrying the scheduled task, roughly 21.5 hours after the intended 00:30 slot -- DO NOT mark 00:30 as tried in timing-intelligence/state.json based on this entry, same reasoning as the 09-08 entry (actual post time too far from assigned slot). linkedin-bot.py --post again exited 1 on the 'Post successful' toast check (same known false-negative as the 09-11 case-study post) but a direct Playwright read of the published-posts page confirmed the post is live with matching text, timestamped 'now' at post time.

posts.engagement_rate_source: socials/scripts/linkedin-bot.py --analytics (standalone Playwright script reading LinkedIn's own Post performance panel)
posts.notes: Catch-up cycle after the 2-day API-credit outage (09-13/09-14) -- fired manually, ahead of the planned 19:30 slot, right after the user asked to post immediately rather than wait. linkedin-bot.py --post failed twice in a row this time (not the usual toast false-negative -- confirmed via the Browser pane that neither attempt actually posted anything). Posted instead via the Browser pane driving the already-logged-in LinkedIn session directly -- first attempt got garbled (rapid batched Return-key + type actions raced and dropped paragraph breaks, merging sentences together), discarded as a draft and redone with the whole post typed as one call with embedded blank lines, which worked cleanly. Confirmed live via the 'Post successful' toast AND the feed showing it as post #1, timestamped 'now'. DO NOT mark 19:30 as tried in timing-intelligence/state.json -- actual post time diverged from the planned slot (fired early by request), same reasoning as prior manual-catch-up entries.

posts.notes: First fully-on-schedule cycle through the new session-based CronCreate pipeline (planned last night, fired automatically at the assigned slot, no manual intervention needed). linkedin-bot.py --post exited 1 on the usual toast false-negative, confirmed genuinely live via the Browser pane against the company admin page (post #1, timestamped 'now', full matching text). First slot marked as a valid timing trial in timing-intelligence/state.json -- actual_post_time matched the scheduled_slot closely enough to count. Sample size is tiny (2 impressions) so the 0.5 engagement rate isn't meaningful on its own yet.
